provenance.scope: Selected Win64 native instructions. Direct E8/E9 scan and statically decoded branches taken when XLua overrides are absent. No runtime test, indirect-call enumeration, or assignment of the five classes to specific skills.

replay.notes: Run with the recorded file fingerprints. Use native.py disasm-at <address> for the additional blocks and for each caller slice beyond the initial unwind entry.

directCallCoverage.scope: Direct E8/E9 candidates only; excludes indirect/virtual calls; instruction boundaries require confirmation.

confirmedCallers.nearPredicate: Distance to m_pullBackDestination <= radius. If that test fails and _notInfluencedByBlock is false, use the source Character blocker range with shrink enabled.
confirmedCallers.nearOutcome: TryEarlyStopPull with the projectile as source until the first success. With _stopAfterPulledBack set, StopMe bypasses StillPull. Otherwise send zero force to StillPull. Each resumed loop checks the position and near predicate again.

confirmedCallers.nearPredicate: Distance to the stored pull point <= 0.05 or source Character blocker range with shrink enabled.
confirmedCallers.nearOutcome: TryEarlyStopPull with the projectile as source until the first success. When the coroutine flag at +0x48 is set, take coroutine cleanup without StillPull. The cleanup either stops the projectile or adjusts its remaining lifetime based on its follow target. With the flag clear send zero force to StillPull.

confirmedCallers.nearPredicate: Distance to the stored pull point <= 0.05, source Character blocker range with shrink enabled, or the behaviour FP timer at +0x38 <= 0.
confirmedCallers.nearOutcome: TryEarlyStopPull with the projectile as source and send zero force to StillPull. The same timer also has an earlier coroutine exit check.

confirmedCallers.nearPredicate: Distance to the current projectile map position <= 0.05. This near branch goes straight from the distance test to the helper and has no blocker-range fallback or second timer test. An earlier per-target FP timer test can exit the continuation.
confirmedCallers.nearOutcome: TryEarlyStopPull with the projectile as source and send zero force to StillPull.
confirmedCallers.continuation: The first-touch marker at coroutine offset 0x38 selects virtual BeginPull (slot 234). Success clears the marker at 0x180dfd5b5. Later resumes use StillPull with the same projectile, and a successful continuation yields state 2 at 0x180dfd92a. The timer-expiry branch tries to clear velocity at 0x180dfd5da and goes to virtual EndPull (slot 235). These instructions prove repeated braking within one coroutine for one target.

confirmedCallers.nearPredicate: Distance to the stored pull point <= 0.05, owner Character blocker range with shrink enabled, or the per-target FP timer <= 0.
confirmedCallers.nearOutcome: TryEarlyStopPull with the owner as source and send zero force to StillPull. The same timer also has an earlier coroutine exit check.

nearRadiusAndBlockShrink.uses: Base radius in all five callers and squared-distance subtraction in the blocker predicate when shrink is enabled.

methods.observation: When initial distance is positive, use min(1, current distance / initial distance)^4.

With _pullToPosInBB set, two successful FP blackboard reads supply the stored pull point. The normal source branch uses source map position plus direction vector times _pullSourceOffset. Without the source object the fallback uses the projectile map position. The near radius uses the flag itself, regardless of which initialization branch supplied the point.
Compare squared map distance against radius squared, inclusive.
When the source Character passes the Unity object test, select 0.05 or zero by the shrink argument and dispatch the blocker range predicate. The four referencing callers pass shrink=true.
Calculate the squared distance between blocker and target map positions. Return d² <= sqrBlockRange() - shrink. The shrink is subtracted from the squared range.

Prune invalid pull sources, require exactly one registered source and a match to the given source, then set rigid-body velocity to zero and return true. Its success tail leaves the matched source registered.
On the accepted path multiply the direction by the submitted force, call AddForce, and return true. Zero submitted force can succeed.
